title: Someone asks for your security code

segments.text: Our staff will never ask you for this code.
A caller claims: "Read me the 6-digit code we texted you so we can secure your account."

flag.reason: The scammer is trying to log into your account and needs this code to get past security.

segments.text: They say your account will be deleted if you do not cooperate immediately.

flag.reason: Threatening account deletion is a pressure tactic to force you to reveal the secret code.

explanation: One-time verification codes are digital keys to your account. When scammers try to break in, the bank sends YOU the code. Scammers then call and ask you to read it to them. Never share a code with anyone.
takeaways: Never share verification codes with anyone.
Banks never ask you for your one-time code.

title: Securing an account that had an unauthorized login
prompt: You receive a genuine alert that someone logged into your email from another state. Put these security steps in order:
steps: Change your email account password to a strong, new passphrase.
Open a new browser window and type the official email service address yourself.
Sign out of all other active sessions and devices in security settings.
Check your account recovery settings to ensure your phone and backup email are still yours.
whyFirstStepMatters: Going directly to the official website by typing the address yourself ensures you do not get tricked by phishing links in fake alert emails.
explanation: When an unauthorized login happens, go directly to the service yourself. Change your password, kick off all active sessions, and verify your backup recovery contact information.
takeaways: Always navigate to account settings directly.
Sign out all existing sessions after changing a password.

title: Identifying a genuine password reset notice
prompt: You receive an email about a password reset that you did not initiate. Which message shows how legitimate companies handle reset requests?

options.label: "A password reset was requested. If you requested this, click here. If you did not make this request, you can safely ignore this message—your account remains secure."
"SECURITY BREACH! An unauthorized device attempted login. Click this link within 10 minutes to verify your identity or your account will be permanently closed."

reasons.a: Correct: Legitimate organizations never penalize you or suspend your account if you ignore a password reset request you did not initiate.
reasons.b: Phishing: Scammers manufacture alarming threats of permanent account termination and tight 10-minute timers to frighten you into clicking imposter login links.

explanation: Authentic web services never threaten to close or suspend accounts if you ignore an unexpected password reset notice. If you ever feel concerned about account safety, open a browser tab and sign into your account directly without clicking links in emails.
takeaways: Legitimate password reset emails state that you can safely ignore them if unrequested.
Never click password links in unexpected emails.
